Explanation of the words:

Ḥā Mīm (ﷺ, not applicable here): This is one of the disjointed letters of the alphabet. It is written thus: حمۤ and pronounced: Ḥāmīm.

Tanzīl al-Kitāb (the revelation of the Book): That is, the Qur'an.

Min Allāh al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥakīm (from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise): That is, from the presence of Allah, the Mighty, the Avenger against His enemies, the Wise in His governance.

Inna fī as-samāwāti wal-arḍ (indeed, in the heavens and the earth): That is, indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth.

La-āyāt (are signs): That is, clear proofs of the existence of Allah, His power, His knowledge and His wisdom, and these necessitate that Lordship and Divinity belong to Him alone, to the exclusion of anything else.

Lil-mu'minīn (for the believers): That is, because they, through faith, are alive; they see and hear, and so they perceive the signs.

Wa fī khalqikum (and in your creation): That is, and in your creation, O people, and the composition of your limbs and the soundness of your structure.

Wa mā batha min dābbah (and what He has scattered of living creatures): That is, and what He has created and dispersed of the various kinds of animals, cattle and others.

Āyāt li-qawmin yūqinūn (are signs for a people who have certainty): That is, signs of Allah's power to resurrect in the Hereafter, since the Creator of these worlds is able to restore them after their death. But these signs are seen only by the people who are certain in their faith in Allah's Lordship, His Divinity, and His attributes of majesty and perfection.

Wakhtilāf al-layli wal-nahār (and the alternation of night and day): That is, by the coming of this and the going of that, and the lengthening of this and the shortening of that, throughout life.

Wa mā anzal Allāh min as-samā'i min rizq (and what Allah sends down from the sky of provision): That is, of rain; rain is called provision because it causes it.

Fa-aḥyā bihi al-arḍa baʿda mawtihā (and gives life thereby to the earth after its death): He gives life by the rain to the earth after its plants have died through drought.

Wa taṣrīf al-riyāḥ (and the turning of the winds): That is, from the east wind to the west wind, from the north to the south, from the scorching wind to the cold, and from the gentle breeze to the violent gale.

Āyāt li-qawmin yaʿqilūn (are signs for a people who reason): That is, in the alternation of night and day, the sending down of rain, the giving of life to the earth, and the turning of the winds, there are clear proofs of the existence of Allah, His power, His knowledge and His wisdom, and that this entails that Lordship and Divinity belong to Allah. "For a people who reason" means those who use their minds to grasp things and to draw conclusions from their premises.

The meaning of the verses:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Ḥā Mīm﴾: Allah knows best what He means by it, for it is among the ambiguous (mutashābih) matters which we are commanded to believe in, entrusting the meaning to the One who revealed them, glorified and exalted is He. We have already mentioned, several times, the two benefits of these disjointed letters, so let it be reviewed in most of the surahs that begin with disjointed letters, such as Ḥā Mīm ad-Dukhān, the surah before this one. And the words of the Exalted, ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾: that is, the revelation of the Qur'an came from Allah, the Mighty, that is, the Avenger against His enemies, the Wise in managing the affairs of His creation. And the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth﴾: that is, in their creation and their origination, and in the wonders of craftsmanship within them, there are signs for the believers, guiding them to the fact that their Lord deserves to be worshipped alone, to the exclusion of all His other creatures. The believers were singled out for these signs because they are alive: they hear, they see, and they reason. So when they look at the heavens and the earth, the realities become manifest to them that the Creator of these worlds can only be All-Powerful, All-Knowing, Wise and Mighty, and therefore He alone must be worshipped, and every worship directed to other than Him is void.

And His words: ﴿And in your creation, O people﴾: that is, in the stages of your creation, from a drop to a clinging clot, to a lump of flesh, to a human being, well-formed, of balanced temperament and composition, possessing hearing, sight, speech and thought.

﴿And what He has scattered of living creatures﴾: that is, what He creates, disperses and spreads across the earth of the various kinds of animals, cattle and living beings of differing kinds, land and sea, are ﴿signs for a people who have certainty﴾: that is, who have certainty in their faith in Allah and His signs, just as they have certainty concerning the established realities of things: one plus one is two, the existent is the opposite of the non-existent, white is other than black, a son must have a father, and sweet is other than bitter. The people of this certainty see in the creation of man and animal signs indicating the existence of Allah, His knowledge, His might, His wisdom, and His power to resurrect and to recompense, which those who lack sound minds among the polytheists and disbelievers deny.

And His words: ﴿And the alternation of night and day﴾: that is, through their succession, by the coming of the night and the going of the day, and the reverse, and by the lengthening of one and the shortening of the other at times, and the reverse likewise. ﴿And what Allah sends down from the sky of provision﴾: that is, of rain, which is the cause of provision, ﴿and gives life thereby to the earth after its death﴾ by the dryness of the plants and their dying upon it. ﴿And the turning of the winds﴾: from the east wind to the west wind, from the north to the south, and from the gentle, soft breeze to the violent gale bearing cold or scorching heat. In the things mentioned are signs, proofs and evidences indicating the existence of the worship of Allah and His oneness in that. ﴿But for a people who reason﴾: that is, for those possessed of bright and sound minds. As for those who have no minds, they see no sign in these or in anything else, let alone signs.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The great status of the noble Qur'an, for it is the revelation of Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.

2- Faith is more general than certainty and precedes it in order, while certainty is higher in rank.

3- The excellence of sound reason when it is employed for good and what benefits.

4- Affirmation of Allah's Divinity through affirmation of His Lordship in creation, governance, knowledge and wisdom.

**Explanation of the words (Sharh al-Kalimat):**

*Allah alladhi sakhkhara lakum al-bahr*: Allah, the God who alone truly deserves worship, not the false gods. *Sakhkhara lakum* means He subjected it for your benefit, making the sea smooth so that wood and similar things float upon it.

*Litajri al-fulk fihi bi-amrih*: He made it thus so that ships sail on it by Allah's permission.

*Wa-litabtaghu min fadlih*: so that you may travel to seek provision from one region to another.

*Wa-la'allakum tashkurun*: in the hope that you will be thankful for Allah's blessings upon you.

*Wa-sakhkhara lakum ma fi as-samawat*: that is, the sun, moon, stars, winds, and rainwater.

*Wa-ma fi al-ard jami'an*: and what is on the earth, including mountains, rivers, trees, and minerals, all from Him, the Exalted.

*Inna fi dhalika la-ayat*: indeed, there are signs, proofs, and evidences of Allah's existence and His divinity.

*Li-qawmin yatafakkarun*: for a people who use their minds and reflect on the existence of these creatures, on who brought them into being, and on why He brought them into being. Thus the realities of Allah's existence, knowledge, power, and mercy become manifest to them, so they believe and affirm His oneness.

*Qul lil-ladhina amanu yaghfiru*: say, O Our Messenger, to the believers among Our servants: let them forgive, that is, overlook and not hold accountable.

*Alladhina la yarjuna ayyam Allah*: those who do not expect the days of Allah, that is, who do not anticipate the days of Allah in which the believers gain the upper hand over them, so that Allah humbles them and grants victory to the believers over them. These are the Messenger and his companions. This was before the command to fight them.

*Liyajzi qawman bima kanu yaksibun*: so that Allah may recompense on the Day of Resurrection a people among them, those whom Allah knew would not believe, for what they earned of harming the Messenger and the believers.

*Man 'amila salihan fali-nafsih*: whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul; that is, it is he who is blessed and made happy by it.

*Wa-man asa'a fa-'alayha*: and whoever does evil, the punishment falls upon him, not upon anyone else.

*Thumma ila rabbikum turja'un*: then to your Lord you will be returned, after death, and He will judge between you concerning the disputes and harm that existed among you.

**The meaning of the verses (Ma'na al-Ayat):**

The noble context continues concerning the guidance of the people of the Prophet ﷺ. Allah's saying ﴿Allah is the One who subjected for you﴾ is a reminder to those who turned away, through proofs and signs that indicate the obligation of faith in Allah, His oneness, and obedience to Him. He informs them that the blessings they have are from Allah, not from those false gods. Allah alone is the One who subjected for you, that is, made subservient, facilitated, and made easy for your benefit, what is in the heavens: the sun, moon, stars, clouds, rain, and winds. He subjected for you what is on the earth: mountains, trees, rivers, seas, minerals, and animals of all kinds. All of this is from Him, and He gave it to you. Indeed, in that which is mentioned of Allah's blessing upon you through all that He subjected for you, there are signs for a people who reflect, so their reflection guides them to the obligation to praise and thank Allah, after they have believed in Him and affirmed His oneness in His lordship and divinity.

As for Allah's saying ﴿Say to those who believe: let them forgive those who do not expect the days of Allah﴾ and the rest of the verse: Allah commands His Messenger to tell his companions, during the days of fear in Mecca before the Hijrah, to pardon and overlook those among the disbelievers of Quraysh who harm them. They should not repay harm with similar harm but should forgive and overlook it. This was abrogated (naskh, the replacement of a ruling by a later one) by the command to fight.

As for His saying ﴿so that He may recompense a people for what they used to earn﴾, it gives the reason for the command to pardon and overlook. That is, Allah postpones their recompense until the Day of Resurrection and rewards them with the worst recompense, because what they earned is among the worst of earnings: harming the Prophet and the believers, the friends of Allah. The indefinite word "a people" indicates that some of them will believe and will not be punished on the Day of Resurrection. Only those who die in disbelief and polytheism among them will be punished.

As for His saying ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul﴾: that is, whoever does righteousness in this worldly life, through faith and obedience to Allah and His Messenger in their commands and prohibitions, purifies his soul by it and becomes fit to enter Paradise. Allah will admit him into Paradise, and his righteous deed returns to him and benefits no one else. Indeed, Allah is free of need from the deeds of His servants. One who does not perform an act cannot purify or cleanse his soul through it. As for His saying ﴿and whoever does evil﴾, that is, during his life, he does not believe and does no righteous deed by which to purify himself. The recompense for his evil earnings, such as polytheism and sins, returns upon himself as punishment in the Fire and eternal abiding therein.

As for His saying ﴿Then to your Lord you will be returned﴾: that is, O people, after this life and what you did in it of good and evil, you will return to Allah on the Day of Resurrection, and He will recompense each of you according to his deeds: good with good, and evil with its like.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 45, verses 16–20:

Explanation of the words:

Al-kitab: that is, the Torah, because it contains the legal rulings of the Shari'ah, unlike the Psalms (al-Zabur) and the Gospel (al-Injil).

Wa al-hukm: that is, the judging of disputes between litigants in a manner that achieves justice.

Wa al-nubuwwah wa razaqnahum min al-tayyibat: that is, We placed prophethood among them, such as the prophethood of Musa, Harun, Dawud and Sulayman, and provided them with good things such as manna and quails and others.

Wa faddalnahum 'ala al-'alamin: that is, above the peoples of their time who were contemporary with them.

Illa min ba'di ma ja'ahumu al-'ilm baghyan baynahum: that is, they did not differ except after knowledge of the sending of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) had come to them, out of rivalry (baghy) among themselves, that is, out of envy of the Arabs, the children of Isma'il, that prophethood should be among them.

Thumma ja'alnaka 'ala shari'atin min al-amr: that is, then We placed you, O Our Messenger, upon a way (shari'ah) of the matter of the true religion which Allah has approved for His servants.

Fa-ttabi'ha: that is, hold fast to following it and walk in its path, for it will lead you to the happiness of both abodes.

Wa la tattabi' ahwa'a alladhina la ya'lamun: from the polytheists of the Arabs and the misguided among the People of the Book.

Innahum lan yughnu 'anka mina Allahi shay'an: that is, if you abandon what has been prescribed for you and follow what they propose you do, which accords with their desires, then indeed, if you follow them, they will not repel from you any of the worldly or otherworldly punishment.

Wa inna al-zalimina ba'duhum awliya'u ba'din: that is, they support one another in this world, but in the Hereafter they will not support one another.

Wa Allahu waliyyu al-muttaqin: that is, He is their protector in all their affairs and their helper against their enemies.

Hadha basa'iru lil-nasi wa hudan wa rahmatun li-qawmin yuqinun: that is, this Qur'an is lights of guidance by which they are guided to what perfects and makes them happy, and a guidance and mercy, but for the people of certainty in their faith. It is they who are guided by it and receive mercy through it. As for those who are not certain, they do not see its guidance nor find its mercy, because their doubt and lack of certainty make it impossible for them to act upon it with earnestness, sincerity and devotion.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues seeking the guidance of the people of the Prophet (ﷺ), presenting to them a situation similar to theirs, so that perhaps they will find in it what reminds and admonishes them, so they believe and worship God alone. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We had certainly given the Children of Israel the Book﴾, that is, We gave the Children of Israel, who are the sons of Ya'qub, titled Isra'il, who was the son of Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful, We gave them ﴿the Book﴾, the Torah, ﴿and judgement﴾, which is understanding of the legal rulings of the Shari'ah and correctness in action, and the truth in it is the fruit of their faith and piety, ﴿and prophethood﴾, so We made from among them prophets and messengers such as Musa, Harun, Yusuf, Dawud, Sulayman and 'Isa; and We preferred them over the worlds, that is, over Pharaoh and his people from the Copts, and over those who lived around their lands among the people, and that was during the days of their faith and uprightness. And We gave them clear proofs of the matter, the matter of religion, carried by the Torah and the Gospel. ﴿But they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them﴾, the divine knowledge carried by the Qur'an and its Prophet. So they disagreed about what they had of the reports concerning the Prophet of the last age, his attributes, and what Allah would bequeath to him and his community of worldly and otherworldly perfection. Rivalry that arose among them, which is envy, drove them to disbelief, so they disbelieved in him and denied him. This verse is similar to the verse in al-Baqarah: ﴿So when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾ [89], and like His saying in Surah al-Bayyinah: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to depart until there came to them clear evidence, a messenger from Allah, reciting purified scriptures﴾ [1–2], and he is Muhammad (ﷺ).

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ﴾, this is a consolation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on one hand, and on the other hand an announcement from Him, the Exalted, that He will judge among them, decide, and repay each one the fruit of his earnings of good and evil in this life, and that will be on the Day of Resurrection.

As for His saying: ﴿Then We placed you on a way of the matter﴾, that is, of the matter of our religion, Islam, which is the religion of the prophets before you, so your Shari'ah did not differ in its foundations from theirs. Therefore, follow it and do not turn aside from it, following the desires of those who do not know: the leaders of Quraysh who present their proposals to you from time to time, nor the desires of the misguided People of the Two Books, the Jews and Christians. They are ignorant; they do not know the guidance of Allah, nor the path of salvation from the Fire and success in Paradise in the Hereafter, nor the path of honour, dignity, dominion and strength in this world.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, they will never avail you against Allah in anything﴾, that is, if you follow their desires and deserve punishment, they will not repel it from you and will not shield you from any of it. As for His saying: ﴿And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another﴾, that is, in this world, so they cooperate in falsehood and evil; but in the Hereafter, one will not help another, nor will they be helped by anyone. ﴿And Allah is the Protector of the righteous﴾: as for the righteous, Allah is their protector in this world and the Hereafter. So hold to the protection of Allah and leave the protection of His enemies, for it will not avail you anything.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿This is insight for mankind﴾, it means the noble Qur'an, which is the eyes of the hearts; by it one perceives what benefits and what harms, and truth from falsehood. Whoever believes in it and acts by what is in it is guided to his happiness and perfection, and whoever does not believe in it nor act by what is in it goes astray and is wretched. And His saying: ﴿And guidance and mercy for a people who are certain﴾, that is, the noble Qur'an is a book of guidance and mercy, by which the guided are guided and the shown mercy are shown mercy, and they are those who are certain of its guidance and mercy, so they act upon it in beliefs, acts of worship, rulings, manners and morals. Thus it was realized for them, just as it was realized for the righteous predecessors of this community. The Qur'an remains a book of guidance and mercy for everyone who believes in it and is certain, and acts upon and applies with earnestness and sincerity its rulings, laws, manners and morals which it brought. The character of the Prophet (ﷺ) was the Qur'an, according to the saying of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, in the authentic report: "His character was the Qur'an."

Guidance from the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Clarification that the disbelief of the People of the Book was out of envy of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his people, the Arabs.

2- Clarification of Allah's bounty upon the Children of Israel in giving them the Book, judgement and prophethood. Yet they differed about the truth out of envy and greed for leadership and for establishing the kingdom of the Children of Israel from the Nile to the Euphrates.

3- Affirmation of resurrection, recompense, prophethood and monotheism.

4- The obligation to adhere to applying the Islamic Shari'ah and not to compromise on any part of it.

5- Affirmation of Allah's protection for the people of faith in Him and piety, by doing what He loves and abandoning what displeases Him.

6- Clarification that the Qur'an is a book of guidance and reform, and nothing in guiding and reforming people is accomplished except through it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 45, verses 24–26:

Explanation of the words:

"And they say: There is nothing but our life of this world": i.e., those who deny the Resurrection said: There is no life but this life, and there is no other life beyond it.

"We die and we live": i.e., some of us die and some of us live, by being born, living, and dying.

"And nothing destroys us but time": i.e., nothing causes us to die except the passage of time over us.

"And they have no knowledge of that": i.e., they have not the slightest knowledge for their saying, neither from revelation nor from a divine Book, nor from sound reason.

"They only conjecture": i.e., they are merely conjecturing, and conjecture has no value and no ruling is built upon it.

"And when Our clear verses are recited to them": i.e., when the verses showing the Resurrection and the other recompense are recited to them plainly.

"Their argument is nothing": i.e., they have no argument except their saying.

"except that they say: Bring back our fathers": i.e., their saying: Bring back to life our fathers who have died, and bring them to us.

"if you are truthful": i.e., if you are truthful in what you tell us about the Resurrection and recompense.

"Say: Allah gives you life, then causes you to die": i.e., say to them, O our Messenger: It is Allah who gave you life when you were dead sperm-drops, and then He causes you to die.

"Then He will gather you to the Day of Resurrection": i.e., then after death He will gather you to the Day of Resurrection for reckoning and recompense.

"About which there is no doubt": i.e., the Day of Resurrection, whose coming at its appointed time is beyond any doubt or uncertainty.

"But most people do not know": i.e., they do not know because they have not received knowledge from divine revelation, due to their disbelief in the messengers and the Books.

Meaning of the verses:

Earlier verses explained the belief of some polytheists that the state of believers and disbelievers is equal on the Day of Resurrection, and that Allah, the Exalted, refuted that belief, rejecting it from them. Here He relates the saying of those who deny the Resurrection altogether, in order to refute them. In this there is a call to all people to faith and righteous deeds for happiness and perfection in both lives, and to Allah belong praise and grace. So the Mighty and Majestic said: "And they say: There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us but time." That is, those who deny the Resurrection and recompense on the Day of Judgment said: There is nothing but this life that we live, and there is no other life beyond it. "We die and we live": that is, we who are alive die, and our children live after us, and thus life continues forever, the elders dying and the young living. "And nothing destroys us but time": that is, nothing causes us to die and perishes us except the passage of time and the length of lifespans. This is complete atheism and a denial of the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, and it is a self-contradiction on their part, for when they are asked who created them, they say Allah, thereby attributing to Him creation, which is the more difficult matter, yet they do not attribute to Him causing death, which is easier than creation. So the Exalted refuted their doctrine of "time" by His saying: "And they have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture." That is, they have no knowledge for this belief of theirs, neither transmitted nor rational; they have not received it from a revelation that Allah inspired to whomever He willed of His servants, nor from sound, correct reason whose judgment is not overturned, such as that one and one make two, and white is the opposite of black, and other rational propositions that cannot be rejected. These materialists have none of that; they have nothing but conjecture and guesswork, and matters of belief are not established by conjecture.

Conjecture is the most false of speech.

And His saying, the Exalted: "And when Our clear verses are recited to them": that is, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recites to them the Qur'anic verses showing the Resurrection and recompense, calling them to believe in it and hold to it. "Their argument is nothing": that is, they have no argument by which to answer what they are called to, except their saying: "Bring back our fathers, if you are truthful": that is, bring to life for us our fathers who have died and present them before us, if you are truthful in what you tell us about the Resurrection and recompense. So the Exalted, in answer to this doubt and to explain the truth in the matter, said: "Say: Allah gives you life, then causes you to die; then He will gather you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt; but most people do not know." That is: say, O our Messenger, to these materialist deniers of the Resurrection: Allah gives you life when you were dead sperm-drops, so He brought you to life, then He causes you to die without your choice. The One who is able to give life and cause death, and who in fact gives life and causes death, is not rendered impossible by reason: He can give life to those whom He gave life to and then caused to die. He has not brought them back to life today as you demanded, because there is no benefit in reviving them after He gave them life and then caused them to die. This is the first point. Second, reviving them for you today would conflict with the lofty wisdom in creating this worldly life and the Hereafter, since they were created to act, and then be recompensed for their deeds, good and evil. For this reason He said: "Then He will gather you," that is, alive on the Day of Resurrection for reckoning and recompense. And His saying "about which there is no doubt" means there is no doubt about its occurrence and coming, since its coming is necessary, the whole of the worldly life being founded upon it. "But most people do not know": this is for two reasons. The first is that they do not reflect or use their reason. The second is that, by denying the divine revelation, they have shut off to themselves the path of sound knowledge, so they do not know, and will not know until they believe in the revelation, hear it, and understand it.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of the Resurrection and recompense.

2- Refutation of the Dahriyyun (the materialists), who attribute life and death to time and deny the existence of the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic.

3- Demonstration that the disbelievers have no rational or transmitted proof for the soundness of disbelief, whether in belief or in action.

4- Allah's not reviving those who demanded the return of the dead so that they would believe was not from incapacity, but because it conflicts with the wisdom upon which the whole universe rests.

5- Demonstration that most people do not know, because they have denied the divine revelation in the Book and the Sunnah.

6- Demonstration that there is no sound knowledge except through the divine revelation.

"And you have no helpers": that is, no helpers who would help you by bringing you out of the Fire.

"That is because you took the signs of God in mockery": that is, that punishment was for you because of your disbelief and your taking the signs of God as a mockery.

"And the worldly life deceived you": that is, the length of life and the enjoyment of desires and pleasures.

"Nor will they be allowed to seek to make amends": that is, they will not be permitted to seek to make amends so that they might repent.

"Then to Allah belongs all praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth": that is, to Allah alone belongs the attribute of beauty, for having carried out His threat against His enemies.

"And to Him belongs majesty throughout the heavens and the earth": that is, the greatness and the executing, enforced rule over whomever He wills.
